title: Make a variable
instructions_md:
## Give a value a name

A **variable** is a name for a value. Use `=` to store a value in it. After that, use the name to get the value back.

```python
city = "Muscat"
print(city)
```

```text
Muscat
```

The name `city` has no quotes. With quotes, Python would print the word `city`.

## Your task

Make a variable called `animal` that holds `falcon`. Then print the variable.
hints: First store the value, then print it.
Use `=` with the name on the left and the string on the right.
Line one stores the string in `animal`. Line two prints `animal` without quotes.
